text.p: A strike by shift workers prevented the restart of France's biggest nuclear reprocessing plant on Monday after a closure for maintenance.

The strikers, among the 1,000 workers who keep the La Hague plant in north-west France running around the clock, want bigger bonuses to compensate for unsociable hours that are now worth 1,000 francs ($160) a month.
On Monday, half of the 120 workers failed to turn up for the first shift after summer maintenance, preventing a planned restart. The strikers normally prepare the spent fuel for chemical treatment.

"The strike will be maintained as long as there are no negotiations with management," said Didier Le Gouestre of the Communist-led CGT union, which called the strike. Management has offered talks in September, after the plant is back to normal.

La Hague, which employs a total of 3,100 people including the shift workers, recovers materials such as plutonium by reprocessing spent nuclear fuel from power stations in nations from Japan to Germany.
